old: A trial in 122 people with dementia found adapted strength training worked whatever their degree of cognitive impairment.
new: A trial in 122 people with mild to moderate dementia found adapted strength training improved strength and chair rises compared with gentle placebo exercise, and the degree of cognitive impairment did not predict who improved.
reason: major: Overstates the trial: the finding is that cognitive impairment did not predict response, not that training 'worked whatever' the impairment; the comparator (placebo exercise) and mild-to-moderate restriction are dropped.

old: People with Alzheimer's disease who forget a physio session can still improve at the movement with practice, a review of lab studies found.
new: A review of 23 lab studies found people with Alzheimer's disease still improved at movement tasks with practice, though more slowly than people without dementia.
reason: major: Population/setting swap: the review studied laboratory motor tasks, not physiotherapy sessions, and found learning below normal levels; attributing a physio-session finding to it is inaccurate.

old: A German trial in 122 people with mild to moderate dementia found that 3 months of adapted strength and balance training improved strength and chair rises.
new: A German trial in 122 people with mild to moderate dementia found that 3 months of adapted strength and balance training improved strength and chair rises compared with gentle placebo exercise.
reason: minor: Comparator missing; reads as within-group change.

old: Rehabilitation trials point the same way.
new: A rehabilitation trial points the same way.
reason: minor: Plural implies several trials; only one trial is cited.

old: Low strength also follows depression, stroke, balance disorders and peripheral vascular disease.
new: Low strength can have other causes, such as depression, stroke, balance disorders or peripheral vascular disease.
reason: minor: Causal/temporal verb stronger than source, which lists these as other possible reasons to consider.

old: Sarcopenia (muscle loss) is found by weakness first.
new: Sarcopenia (loss of muscle strength and mass) is found by weakness first.
reason: minor: Gloss 'muscle loss' conflicts with the strength-first definition used in the same post and in the other versions.

old: About 3 in 10 older people admitted to acute hospital leave less able to wash, dress, use the toilet or get in and out of a bed or chair than before they became ill, a 2020 pooled analysis found.

reason: minor: The 30% pooled figure uses baselines taken before or at admission; 'before they became ill' fits only the 2-week pre-admission sensitivity analysis (33%). Same wording in threads.

reason: minor: No comparator: presents within-arm change without the control arm.
